results.name: Late Pre-Roman Bowl
results.description:
This bowl with an X-shaped handle can be dated to c. 50 BC-200 AD, i.e., [Late Pre-Roman Iron Age or Early Roman Iron Age](https://bit.ly/3vucSEX). It was found in [Gårdby parish](https://bit.ly/3hrP1gS) on the island of Öland. It belongs to a type of fine ware with carefully polished surface and a delicately incised décor. The black surface is a result of firing in a reducing atmosphere, in other words, the oxygen supply has been restricted during the firing. It is made in a style typical for Southern Scandinavia, Northern Germany and Poland. The bowl has probably been used as a drinking vessel at feasts, dinners and during rituals.

Online Collections: [580574_HST](https://bit.ly/3stKKjB)

results.name: Mina'i ware bowl, 1200-1299 CE
results.description:
Iranian Mina'i ware bowl, 1200-1299 CE, now in the collection of the Minneapolis Institute of Art.


From the bowl's description on [artsmia.org](www.artsmia.org):

*'The theme of two horsemen on either side of a tree frequently appears on mina'i ware. It might have alluded to a hunt scene, a luxury enjoyed by the princely classes.'*


More information [here](https://collections.artsmia.org/art/1085/minai-ware-bowl-iran)

results.name: Winter Bowl
results.description:
Practicing Blender particle systems by amking a simple little snowflake patterned bowl. 

The snowflake particle was made by link-duplicating a plane and trotating it 5 times to fit into 6 degrees symetry, then extruding, splitting and merging verts into a snowflake shape. After merging and removing duplicates this was then used by the particlke system to cover a weight painted portion of the bowl model [deformed and loop cut cylender mesh] with a scattering of snowflakes. Rotation options allowed the snowflakes to stick out along the normals of the bowl faces.

results.name: Popcorn Bowl
results.description:
Made from 321 photos in 3DF Zephyr.

I decided to make this model out of a passion for popcorn. Only the best 100% handmade popcorn was used to make this prop for scanning. And a dozens of grams of hot glue.


1 popcorn flake is glued to the bowl

1 popcorn flake!

Heat up glue gun, squeeze some glue down

2 popcorn flakes are glued to the bowl...


Only the top layer is glued. Bottom layers are sealed with a cardboard cover. The bowl is a bit transparent and now you can see that there's popcorn insde.

The bowl itself was also prepared for scanning - it was painted for better reconstruction. It didn't help very much though. Popcorn appeared very well after tweaking the photoconsistency parameters but bowl always had bumpy and uneven surface. It took a lot of work to separately patch/smooth/retopology only the bowl. Every action could shrink or distort the bowl.

There're still places between popcorn and bowl with bad geometry but you can cover it with separate model of [popcorn flake](https://skfb.ly/6UwV9)
